title: Cozze al Vino Bianco
subtitle: Mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic, and parsley
excerpt: Cozze al vino bianco are mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic, and parsley with no tomato. The broth is clean, briny, and aromatic. It is faster than the tomato version and lets the flavour of the mussels come through more clearly.
sourceNotes: Steamed mussels in white wine is a preparation common to the entire Mediterranean coastline. The Italian version differs from the French moules mariniere primarily in the amount of butter and cream used: the Italian preparation uses only olive oil, no butter or cream. It is associated particularly with Ligurian and Sardinian cooking, where the dry local white wines are a natural complement to shellfish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Clean the mussels up to 1 hour ahead. Cook and serve immediately.

content.text: Cozze al vino bianco are mussels opened in white wine with garlic, olive oil, and parsley. No tomato, no cream. The broth is the liquid from the wine, the olive oil, and the juice released by the mussels as they open: briny, garlicky, and light. It is one of the fastest ways to make a dish that looks and tastes impressive. The whole thing from pot to table takes under 15 minutes.

items.prepNote: scrubbed, beards removed, any open ones discarded

content.text: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes until pale gold.
Increase the heat to high. Add the white wine and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Tip in all the mussels and put the lid on. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until all the mussels have opened. Discard any that remain closed.
Scatter the parsley and add a crack of black pepper. Serve immediately in deep bowls with the broth poured over and lemon wedges alongside.

This preparation is Italian in its use of olive oil only and its lack of cream. It is common along the Ligurian coast, where the local dry white wines (Vermentino, Pigato) are used in the cooking liquid. The no-tomato version shows the mussel flavour more clearly than the tomato version and is often preferred by those who want to taste the shellfish rather than the sauce.
